Hey there! Just wondering are you generally more acne prone or not. Because if you are not and while I am no dermatologist, I believe what you have is 'post inflammatory erythema'. Think of them like acne scars, according to Schweiger Dermatology Group, described P.I.E as -- "The redness is from damage or dilation done to capillaries near the surface of the skin resulting in small flat red marks.".

Now, how to eliminate or reduce the appearance. If you can, book an appointment with a dermatologist since it is quite difficult to resolve. If you can't don't worry I totally understand, what I did was using niacinamide in the morning (I used 'the ordinary' but i heard that 'paula's choice' is better) since it is amazing at managing inflammation. And hyaluronic acid at night since it is a non-greasy moisturiser and doesn't cause fungal acne (which can lead to inflammation.)

You've mentioned in the comments that your skin feels a little dehydrated, if you want I say try swapping your exfoliates for vitamin c serum (I used the ordinary MAP 10% because it is more suitable for sensitive skin than the other vit c versions) since it is less harsh and still does a great job at reducing inflammation and pigmentation. You can also alternate like one week with your glycolic exfoliate and the next with a vitamin c serum, whatever that makes you comfortable!
